title: MongoDB Relationships
summary: Choose embedded data or references before learning multi-document transactions.

richText: Embedding and references
Embedding stores a related object inside the same document. A reference points to another document stored separately.
Use embedding for small data owned by one document and usually read with it. One write can change the parent and embedded data together.
Use references when related documents are queried separately, have their own lifecycle or would make the parent grow without a useful bound.
MongoDB references do not provide JPA relationships, foreign-key enforcement or automatic cascade saves.
Map a database reference
@DBRef stores a MongoDB database reference and resolves it into the referenced Java object when needed.
DBRef resolution is eager by default. lazy=true requests deferred loading.
@DocumentReference is another Spring Data option. Its default stored representation uses the referenced document ID.
Both options require an explicit policy for saving and deleting referenced documents.

example.title: Store journal entry references on a user
description: Use JournalEntry from the document mapping page.
This case keeps entries in journal_entries and their references in users.
Put User.java and UserRepository.java under the application package.
explanation: User stores references to journal entries instead of embedding their content.
Saving User does not automatically save new entries in its list.
Loading a user resolves its entry references by default.

richText: Save referenced documents
Save a new referenced document before saving the reference to it.
Writes to separate documents are separate operations unless they participate in a transaction.
Deleting a referenced document does not automatically remove its stored references. Define cleanup for both sides.

example.title: Save an entry and its user reference
description: Run this code inside a service with journalRepository and userRepository injected.
user is an existing User. entry is a new JournalEntry.
explanation: The first write saves the entry and obtains its ID.
The second write stores the reference on User.
If the second write fails without a transaction, the entry can remain saved without the reference.

richText: Growing collections and permissions
Resolving many references increases database work. Lazy loading defers this work but does not remove it.
For a growing journal, store userId on each entry and query entries by userId. This avoids keeping an ever-growing list on User.
Use bounded queries or pages when reading many entries.
A stored relationship does not grant permission. Reads and changes must check the authenticated owner.
